newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Jefferies to grow its banking.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Jefferies to grow its banking.

text.p: Jefferies Group Inc, a firm built on its institutional trading business, plans to expand its investment banking operations, focusing on mid-sized companies in eight industries, its chief executive said on Tuesday.
The investment banking side accounted for about 25 percent of the firm's total 1996 revenue of $540.8 million, chief executive Frank Baxter said in an interview.
He declined to give a specific forecast, but said "it will, under any circumstances, be a higher percentage in 1997."
The industries it is focusing on are energy, health care, gaming, business services, retail, telecommunications, real estate investment trusts, and financial services, he said.
Jefferies plans to employ a strategy analogous to the one used to build its trading, he said.

"We think the growth we experienced in the previous 30 years in finding a relationship between institutions can be replicated -- more than replicated -- by working out a relationship between institutions and corporations," Baxter said.

Baxter expressed confidence that the firm would be able to develop its niche amid ongoing consolidation in the brokerage industry, highlighted by the recent tie-up between Dean Witter Discover & Co and Morgan Stanley Group Inc.
"There's no apparent advantage to having size," he said.

But he did add that "there's a lot to be said" for alliances such as the deal struck between Salomon Inc and Fidelity Investments that gave Salomon's corporate finance clients exclusive access to Fidelity's retail brokerage and mutual fund clients.
Baxter said Jefferies expected strength in the firm's initial public offering business this year, provided strong market conditions prevail.
"Given a decent market, things look extremely good for us," he said.
